page_hint: Ch 25 §8 mini-case, ADR 0017 Consequences, 'Fleet-level effect' bullet
quoted_clause: the peak KV-residency screen moves from 21 hosts to ~11 (344 in-flight ÷ 35.0 concurrent per host = 9.8, +N−1)
observed: Compares raw FP16 screen (21, no +N−1) against FP8 screen including +N−1 (10+1=11). The 21 from Ch 20 is the raw screen: ⌈344/17⌉ = 21. Applying +N−1 to FP16 gives 22. The correct like-for-like comparison is either raw 21→10 or +N−1 22→11.
correction: State either 'from 21 to 10 (raw screens)' or 'from 22 to 11 (+N−1 screens)' — apply the same policy basis to both sides.
acceptance_test: Both sides of the 'from X to Y' comparison use the same policy basis (both raw, or both with +N−1).
verdict_evidence: ch25:264 'from 21 hosts to ~11 (344/35.0=9.8, +N-1)'; 21 raw screen, 11 = ceil(9.8)+1; FP16 +N-1 is 22; bases differ across sides.
fix_instruction: Make both sides the same basis: 'from 21 to 10 (raw screens)' or 'from 22 to 11 (+N-1 screens)'.

quoted_clause: its decision body is kept, not rewritten — the status is updated to superseded, with a link to the successor
observed: The record immediately below has Status: HOLD — screened, not committed. The parenthetical says the status is updated to superseded, which contradicts the displayed HOLD status.
correction: Change to 'if and when superseded, the status is updated to superseded with a link to the successor' or remove the clause. Keep the displayed status HOLD.
acceptance_test: The prose and the Status field agree: ADR 0015 is HOLD now; supersession is described conditionally.
verdict_evidence: ch25:188 HOLD record yet 'status is updated to superseded'; :192 'Status: HOLD' and :194 'No delivery mode is committed'; no supersession occurred.
fix_instruction: Make it conditional: 'when superseded, the body is kept and the Status line is updated, with a link to the successor.' Keep :192 HOLD.

page_hint: Chapter 25, Architect’s Question and ADR 0016 Consequences
quoted_clause: Accepted, this record sets the canonical deployment's precision label to BF16; because FP16 and BF16 are both 2 B/parameter, every footprint, KV and cost figure in this handbook is unchanged.
observed: The chapter opening calls the canonical system “a 70B dense FP16 deployment (FP16 label; see ADR 0016),” but ADR 0016 says the accepted record sets the canonical deployment’s precision label to BF16. This leaves the reader unsure whether the canonical label is FP16, BF16, or a generic 16-bit label.
correction: Align the two statements. For example: opening: “a 70B dense 16-bit deployment (BF16 per ADR 0016; FP16/BF16 footprints are identical, so the book’s 16-bit arithmetic is unchanged)”; or ADR 0016: “sets the canonical runtime precision to BF16; the book’s 16-bit footprint label remains FP16/BF16-equivalent.” Ensure all “FP16 deployment” references are either qualified or changed to “16-bit (BF16).”
acceptance_test: A reader can state unambiguously whether the canonical deployment is labeled FP16, BF16, or 16-bit, and why the arithmetic is unchanged.
verdict_evidence: ch25:5 '70B dense FP16 deployment (FP16 label; see ADR 0016)' vs ch25:57 'sets the canonical deployment's precision label to BF16'; same chapter, opposite labels.
fix_instruction: ch25:57 - 'sets the canonical runtime precision to BF16; the 16-bit footprint label stays FP16 (both 2 B/param), so no figure changes'.

page_hint: Ch 25 §1 Concept (status list) and §3.1 template ("## Status" block)
quoted_clause:
**Title** and status (proposed, accepted, superseded, deprecated) ... ## Status
<proposed | accepted | superseded | deprecated>  (date)
observed: The chapter's status vocabulary has four values, but the chapter's own worked HOLD record and the §6 callout both instruct the reader to write "HOLD" into the Status field, and Ch 22 §6's ADR 0015 excerpt does exactly that. The template a reader is told to copy does not permit the value the chapter tells them to use.
correction: Add HOLD to both lists: "status (proposed, accepted, hold, superseded, deprecated)" and "<proposed | accepted | hold | superseded | deprecated>  (date)", with one clause defining HOLD as "screened, not committed, with named exit criteria".
acceptance_test: Every status value used anywhere in Ch 22 or Ch 25 is one of the enumerated values in §1 and is permitted by the §3.1 template.
verdict_evidence: ch25:11 and :79 template allow four statuses; :186 tells reader to write HOLD and :192 records 'Status: HOLD — screened, not committed'.
fix_instruction: Add hold to ch25:11 and the :79 placeholder, with one clause defining HOLD as screened-not-committed with named exit criteria.
